newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says sees no need to change M3 definition.
newsitem.headline: Buba says sees no need to change M3 definition.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that although savings accounts bearing a notice period had become more important in Germany in recent years, it saw no need to change the definition of M3 money supply as a result.

In its May monthly report, the central bank noted that better conditions attached to such savings accounts -- partly due to competition for business within the banking sector -- had helped to increase their popularity.

But it said although such forms of investment had to some extent taken on the character of monetary capital investment -- meaning that money was parked there long-term -- this was taking place only gradually and there had been no clear switch to use these investment forms for thst purpose.

It therefore saw no need to redefine M3 money supply -- the central bank's main monetary policy indicator -- which comprises cash in circulation, sight deposits and term deposits of up four years in addition to the savings accounts.
The central bank targets M3 for its policy on the basis that growth in the money supply provides an indication of future inflation trends.
"At the moment there is no reason to change the definition...of M3," the central bank said.
"This is even more true given that the majority of econometric studies continue to come to the conclusion that demand for money in Germany is stable in the long term."
The bank said it was continuing to observe the situation, warning that the change in savings patterns meant the division between money and monetary capital had been blurred.
M3 is intended to measure only forms of investment that are relatively close to cash because they can be liquidated relatively easily.

The Bundesbank rejected proposals to exclude short-term investments under special conditions from M3 as erroneous or at least premature. It said it appeared at the moment such investments were attracting funds that had formerly been parked in another M3 component account.
